title: Sonny and the Falling Leaf | Bedtime Story
description: Join Sonny the quokka as she watches golden autumn leaves drift softly down from a gum tree and discovers that letting go is the most peaceful feeling in the world. A soothing story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales, perfect for settling little ones to sleep.
narration:
The sun was starting to go down behind the tall gum trees, and the whole bush was turning golden and warm. Little Sonny the quokka sat in her favourite mossy spot and looked up at the big old gum tree above her.

One by one, the leaves were letting go. They didn't fall quickly — they drifted, slowly, slowly, turning gently in the soft evening air. Golden and brown and the colour of honey.

Sunny watched one leaf for a long time. She saw it leave its branch so quietly, as if it wasn't scared at all. As if letting go was the easiest, most peaceful thing in the world.

She thought about that. When she was sleepy at the end of the day, she sometimes tried to hold on — to stay awake, to keep her eyes open just a little longer. But maybe, like the leaf, letting go was the softer way.

Another leaf drifted down, spinning slowly, and landed right beside her little round ear. She reached out and caught it — just barely — before it touched the ground. It was soft and dry and smelled like the whole bush at the end of summer.

Sunny held the leaf close. She curled up small in the mossy warmth, tucking the leaf gently under her chin. The gum tree rustled above her, sending more leaves drifting down like little golden whispers.

Her eyes grew heavy. Her breathing slowed. And just like the leaf, she let go — softly, slowly — and drifted off to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little golden leaf. Goodnight, little one.
